headline: Western Connecticut sets the LEC pace
dek: Western Connecticut went through conference play without a defeat, finishing the full season with fourteen wins, five draws, and four losses. Across all matches, the program scored 54 goals, outscoring Eastern Connecticut, Keene State, and VTSU Castleton combined while conceding 24.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Goal production split the league into clear tiers, with UMass Boston's 44 goals alone topping the combined totals of Eastern Connecticut and Keene State while Western Connecticut sat further ahead.

wire.line: Non-conference play ended with 34 wins, eighteen draws, and 36 losses, yet 145 goals scored against 142 conceded.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Western Connecticut midfielder Nickolas Santana led the conference in scoring with thirteen goals and five assists on 43 shots.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: UMass Boston spread its attack across at least thirteen distinct scorers on the way to twelve wins, one draw, and six losses.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: Southern Maine relied on a narrow attacking rotation, with at least six distinct scorers accounting for its 29 goals across all matches.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Eastern Connecticut goalkeeper Jack Harmon posted a 0.877 save percentage, making 71 saves while allowing ten goals.

last_match.line: The defeat ended a winning run for UMass Boston and closed the conference's season.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
